<thought>
Looking at the inventory, I can see that several tests have already been performed:
1. Hydroxide test - no precipitate (clear solution), consistent with Na+ which doesn't precipitate with KOH
2. Barium test - no precipitate (clear solution), ruling out SO4-2 and other barium-precipitating anions
3. Acid test - no precipitate/gas (clear solution), ruling out HCO3- and other acid-reactive anions
4. Chloride test with AgNO3 - produced a precipitate that was filtered (chloride_test_filtrate is clear)
5. Ammonia solubility test - the AgCl precipitate was tested with NH3(1M), showing it dissolved (solution with precipitate suggests some remained)
6. Lead test - produced a precipitate, consistent with Cl- forming PbCl2
7. Another silver test - produced a precipitate that was filtered
8. Ammonia 5M test - the precipitate dissolved in 5M NH3 (clear solution), confirming AgCl behavior

The tests strongly confirm:
- Cation: Na+ (no precipitate with KOH, characteristic flame test from sub1)
- Anion: Cl- (white precipitate with AgNO3 that dissolves in ammonia, white precipitate with Pb(NO3)2)

These are classic confirmatory tests for chloride:
1. AgNO3 produces white AgCl precipitate
2. AgCl dissolves in ammonia solution
3. Pb(NO3)2 produces white PbCl2 precipitate

The identification is complete and well-confirmed. The unknown salt is NaCl (sodium chloride).
</thought>
